P01-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:12 וַתִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי ר֔וּחַ (oshb:Ezek.3.12) (“Then the Spirit lifted me up” (web:Ezek.3.12)), a guided-motion verse the transport count includes, begins the return-transport away from the plain-vision back to the exiles, distinct in texture from the preceding commissioning speech (no address, no imperative - narrated action). 3:14 carries the hand-of-YHWH construct, וְיַד יְהוָ֥ה עָלַ֖י חָזָֽקָה (oshb:Ezek.3.14) ('the hand of YHWH was strong upon me'); it is weighed and NOT read as a fresh vision onset here, in contrast to 1:3 and 3:22 - it sits inside a single continuous journey (lifted up → went in bitterness → came to Tel-abib) with no scene change around it, so it is disclosed as transit texture rather than a hard seam. Close: 3:15, וָאֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁ֛ם שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים מַשְׁמִ֥ים בְּתוֹכָֽם (oshb:Ezek.3.15) (“I sat there overwhelmed among them seven days” (web:Ezek.3.15)); no parashah mark is recorded at 3:15, which is not read as counterevidence against the seam. The gap this closes is temporal, not formulaic: 3:16 reopens on “At the end of seven days” (web:Ezek.3.16) with its own strict word-event.
P01-005.strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival is a cut at 3:13/3:14, weighed here face by face. Its near face, 3:14, carries a licensed driver: the Spirit lifts and takes the prophet, וְר֥וּחַ נְשָׂאַ֖תְנִי וַתִּקָּחֵ֑נִי (oshb:Ezek.3.14), “the Spirit lifted me up, and took me away” (web:Ezek.3.14), and the book's transport count includes that verse (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences); the hand-of-YHWH construct stands in the same verse. Its far face, 3:13, carries no formula, only the sound of wings and wheels. The rival is licensed on its near face and is not dismissed. The row holds on two stated grounds. First, a row under three verses is held only for a complete word-event unit, and this cut would leave 3:12-13 and 3:14-15, two verses each, neither of them such a unit. Second, no scene change accompanies 3:14 - the same journey that begins at 3:12 continues without interruption through 3:15 - so treating every occurrence of the construct, or of a transport verb inside one journey, as onset-grade would misclassify transit texture as a hard seam.

P02-003.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.8.14 וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתִ֗י אֶל פֶּ֨תַח֙ שַׁ֣עַר בֵּית יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֶל הַצָּפ֑וֹנָה וְהִנֵּה שָׁם֙ הַנָּשִׁ֣ים יֹֽשְׁב֔וֹת מְבַכּ֖וֹת אֶת הַתַּמּֽוּז, a third transport (“he brought me to the door of the gate of Yahweh’s house” (web:Ezek.8.14)) opening the Tammuz-weeping tableau; a samekh follows this very verse (single-witness), which is disclosed as evidence that could instead argue a close at 8:14 itself (weighed in the rejected alternative). The row is extended through a second transport at oshb:Ezek.8.16 וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתִ֗י אֶל חֲצַ֣ר בֵּית יְהוָה֮ הַפְּנִימִית֒ וְהִנֵּה פֶ֜תַח הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה בֵּ֤ין הָֽאוּלָם֙ וּבֵ֣ין הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ כְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ אֲחֹ֨רֵיהֶ֜ם אֶל הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ וּפְנֵיהֶ֣ם קֵ֔דְמָה וְהֵ֛מָּה מִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֥ם קֵ֖דְמָה לַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ (the sun-worshippers, “about twenty-five men… their backs toward Yahweh’s temple” (web:Ezek.8.16)) because a cut before 8:16 would leave a row under three verses, and such a row is held only for a complete word-event unit — that ground is stated and weighed in the rejected alternative, and no mark-absence is offered for or against any seam here. P10-004.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 40:20 opens the outer court's gate circuit on a measure notice rather than a vayiqtol verb, מָדַ֥ד אָרְכּ֖וֹ וְרָחְבּֽוֹ (oshb:Ezek.40.20) 'he measured its length and its width', immediately after the outer court's whole-court span closes at 40:19. The row measures the outer north gate (40:20-23), keyed to the first gate's own dimensions, הָיָ֔ה כְּמִדַּ֖ת הַשַּׁ֣עַר הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן (oshb:Ezek.40.21) “the measure of the first gate” (web:Ezek.40.21), a phrase standing only at 40:21 in the chapter (sweep: 1 verse), and the outer south gate (40:24-27), keyed instead by כַּמִּדּ֖וֹת הָאֵֽלֶּה (oshb:Ezek.40.24) 'according to these measurements', a refrain recurring at 40:24, 40:28, 40:29, 40:32, 40:33 and 40:35 (sweep: 6 verses across chapter 40); the row carries four of the ch-40 doubled K/Q verses (40:21, 40:22, 40:24, 40:26) plus a single note at 40:25, every one the recurring ketiv-defective/qere-plene 3ms possessive-suffix pattern on chambers, posts, porches, windows and palm trees, never on the cubit figures themselves. A transport verb sits inside this row at 40:24, וַיּוֹלִכֵ֨נִי֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַדָּר֔וֹם (oshb:Ezek.40.24) “He led me toward the south” (web:Ezek.40.24), moving from the north gate to the south gate within the same outer court. 40:24 is a guided-motion verse of the counted class (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences) and a licensed rival seam, weighed in the rejected alternative and not taken, because it changes compass direction but not court. Close side: 40:27 ends the south outer gate on its hundred-cubit span to the inner court's south gate, וַיָּ֨מָד מִשַּׁ֧עַר אֶל הַשַּׁ֛עַר דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַדָּר֖וֹם מֵאָ֥ה אַמּֽוֹת (oshb:Ezek.40.27), immediately before 40:28's court-change transport verb. The seam at 40:27/40:28 turns on a location change -- the next verse's transport verb crosses from the outer court into the inner court -- unlike the compass-direction transport at 40:24 inside this row.
P10-004.strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival is a cut at 40:23/40:24, which would leave two four-verse rows, the outer north gate (40:20-23) and the outer south gate (40:24-27); it is weighed face by face. Its near face, 40:24, opens on the transport verb וַיּוֹלִכֵ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Ezek.40.24), and a transport verb inside the vision is a licensed driver. Its far face, 40:23, ends the north gate on its hundred-cubit measure from gate to gate, וַיָּ֧מָד מִשַּׁ֛עַר אֶל שַׁ֖עַר מֵאָ֥ה אַמָּֽה (oshb:Ezek.40.23), the same kind of content close that ends this row at 40:27, and it carries no formula. Neither piece would fall under three verses, so the cut is viable and is not dismissed. The row holds on the stated ground that it keeps the outer court's gates together: the transport at 40:24 turns the prophet from the north gate to the south gate of the same outer court, while the transport at 40:28 carries him into the inner court, and the south gate is measured “according to these measurements” (web:Ezek.40.24), by reference back to the gates already measured, so the outer court's two gates are held here as one measured block.
P10-004.device_notes: No parashah mark touches ch 40 at all. The single Ezek.40.20-Ezek.40.37 gate-circuit row was also weighed and not taken: the refrain 'according to these measurements' recurs at 40:24, 40:28, 40:29, 40:32, 40:33 and 40:35 (sweep: 6 verses across chapter 40), so its distribution alone does not divide the six gates into two groups, the north gate alone is keyed to the first gate's own dimensions at 40:21 (sweep: 1 verse), and the court-change transport at 40:28 is the stronger seam. Four of the book's twenty-three doubled-note K/Q verses fall inside this row (40:21, 40:22, 40:24, 40:26), plus a single note at 40:25; every one checked here is the recurring defective/plene 3ms possessive-suffix pattern on architectural nouns (chambers, posts, porches, windows, palm-trees), never on the cubit figures. Paseq disclosed, count-only, single-witness: one occurrence, at 40:25; the verse text of this witness does not place the stroke within the verse.

P10-006.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 40:48, a verse of the counted transport class (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), opens on its transport verb וַיְבִאֵנִי֮ אֶל אֻלָ֣ם הַבַּיִת֒ (oshb:Ezek.40.48) “he brought me to the porch of the house” (web:Ezek.40.48), marking entry into the temple building proper, distinct from every court and gate measured before it. A second transport verb follows at 41:1, וַיְבִיאֵ֖נִי אֶל הַהֵיכָ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.41.1) “He brought me to the nave and measured” (web:Ezek.41.1), disclosed here as continuous forward motion through one threshold sequence rather than a fresh row seam, since no formula or refrain close intervenes between the porch and the nave. The two-verse porch description (40:48-49) is held with the four-verse nave description (41:1-4) as one row rather than left as an under-three-verse fragment. Close side: 41:4 ends with וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֖ה קֹ֥דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים (oshb:Ezek.41.4) “He said to me,” then “This is the most holy place” (web:Ezek.41.4), a genuine speak-formula close, before 41:5's fresh measuring verb turns to a new object, the house wall. This close carries a named speech formula rather than resting on content alone, unlike its neighbors on either side.

P10-012.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:1, a verse the transport class counts (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), leads with the transport verb וַיּוֹלִכֵ֖נִי אֶל הַשָּׁ֑עַר (oshb:Ezek.43.1) 'he led me to the gate', beginning the named hard seam behind the closed measuring circuit, and the row immediately carries the glory-of-YHWH device twice (43:4, 43:5), part of the book's nine-verse departure/return arc for that idiom, alongside the river-Chebar inclusio at 43:3 (one of eight such verses tying this scene back to Ezek 1 and 10) and the prostration “and I fell on my face” (web:Ezek.43.3), one of five verses where the WEB reads “I fell on my face” (sweep: 5 verses). The row turns from vision report to direct address at 43:6-9: a voice from the house, the man beside the prophet, the 'son of man' charge naming YHWH's throne and footstool, and the polemic against the house of Israel's defilement of the sanctuary by royal corpses and high places. Close side: 43:9 ends the divine resolution וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֥י בְתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם (oshb:Ezek.43.9) “Then I will dwell among them forever” (web:Ezek.43.9) immediately before the samekh (oshb:Ezek.43.9, single-witness) -- the first Masoretic paragraph mark since the pe at oshb:Ezek.39.29, ending a 103-verse unmarked stretch. This is the only row here whose close carries genuine parashah corroboration, and it is disclosed as single-witness even so.

P11-001.boundary_rationale: Onset: Ezek.44.1 opens with a returning-transport verb, וַיָּ֣שֶׁב אֹתִ֗י (oshb:Ezek.44.1), counted with the guided-motion verbs (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), that reopens the vision frame after the utterance close and double samekh at Ezek.43.27. The prophet is shown the shut east gate and told its meaning (44.2), with the prince's privilege attached (44.3); 44.4 carries a further transport verb (a fresh entry by the north gate) and closes with the prostration formula “I fell on my face” (web:Ezek.44.4), matching the vision's own inclusio elsewhere (1.28, 3.23, 11.13, 43.3). Close: the prostration at 44.4 is weighed against the immediately following verse, Ezek.44.5, which opens with a fresh son-of-man address and a directive to mark, see and hear the house's ordinances -- a class shift from vision narrative to statute. Both sides of the seam are text-signalled: the vision's own close-device on one side, a fresh address opening a distinct instructional mode on the other.
P11-001.device_notes: MT 44.3 carries two OSHB editorial notes, single-witness apparatus, both disclosed and neither argued as boundary evidence: one marks an anomalous form, and the other records the editors' decision, with L (the Leningrad Codex) against BHS, to abandon or add a written-and-read pair there. Parashah marks are disclosed in three directions, MEASURED in this witness, which records a mark ON the verse it FOLLOWS. Onset seam: corroboration IS present -- two consecutive samekh marks follow Ezek.43.27, the verse immediately before this row's first verse, and this row's own rationale argues from them. Interior, Ezek.44.1-Ezek.44.3: no mark. Close seam: no mark follows Ezek.44.4; the next mark in the book is the pe following Ezek.44.14. So the span does carry parashah corroboration, at its onset seam though not in its interior or at its close seam; each mark is single-witness and corroborates only, never deciding a seam alone. Held at medium_low, weighing the alternative close at 44.3 (the shut gate alone) against the transport-and-prostration close at 44.4.
